{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZf3MiQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDHBco", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 69, "title": "Implement V30 maskable-interrupt inhibition after documented segment MOV and POP instructions", "body": "## Problem

The VM profile can acknowledge a maskable hardware interrupt too early after segment-register instructions. This affects DOS code that relies on the V30's documented instruction-boundary guarantees.

At baseline `ea2713b51a94a53232448b622f35dcb2e01b2fac`, [Cpu::step](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/ea2713b51a94a53232448b622f35dcb2e01b2fac/src/cpu.rs#L617) checks the PIC before executing an instruction unless `inhibit` is set. However:

- The [segment POP decoder](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/ea2713b51a94a53232448b622f35dcb2e01b2fac/src/cpu.rs#L1039) sets inhibition only for SS.
- The [segment MOV decoder](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/ea2713b51a94a53232448b622f35dcb2e01b2fac/src/cpu.rs#L1238) sets inhibition only when writing SS; segment reads never set it.

Consequently, documented non-SS forms do not protect the following instruction. This is a source-established gap; the evaluator has not executed a reproduction.

## Expected outcome

Implement the missing **VM maskable-INT inhibition** for documented segment MOV/POP forms, using the existing CPU interrupt mechanism.

The authoritative contract is NEC's **V20/V30 User's Manual**, Chapter 6, printed page **6-4**, “Interrupt Disable Timing.” It lists MOVs in both directions between segment registers and register/memory operands, plus segment POPs, as boundaries at which INT acknowledgement is inhibited before the following instruction. This applies beyond SS. See the [original NEC manual](https://www.dosdays.co.uk/media/nec/NEC-V20-V30-Users-Manual.pdf), also available through this [scan mirror](https://ftpmirror.your.org/pub/misc/bitsavers/pdf/nec/V20_V30_Users_Manual_Oct86.pdf).

Cover documented MOV destinations ES/SS/DS, MOV sources ES/CS/SS/DS, and POP ES/SS/DS. Inhibition must delay acknowledgement without clearing IF or consuming the PIC request. Consecutive qualifying instructions renew the protected boundary. Prefixes remain part of their instruction.

**Focused scope:** maskable interrupt acknowledgement after these instructions, with ordinary non-REP following instructions providing the focused acceptance contract. Preserve Ap behavior, existing STI/SS behavior, operand results, flags, and scheduler budgets.

**Non-goals:** VM TF traps, NMI delivery, undocumented MOV-to-CS/POP-CS forms, new REP-boundary semantics, protected execution, paging, x87, and unrelated PIC changes. Existing REP interruption checks remain mandatory regressions; their passing does not verify every segment-shadow/REP interaction.

## Context and reproduction

A deterministic native reproduction can:

1. Configure VM code containing `MOV DS,AX; INC BX; NOP`, with IF set and a valid interrupt stack/vector.
2. Execute the MOV with no pending request.
3. Request an unmasked PIC IRQ through the existing native device interface.
4. Step once and inspect BX, CS:IP, and PIC IRR/ISR.

Current source permits acknowledgement before `INC BX`. Expected behavior executes the increment first, leaves the request pending during that step, and acknowledges it at the next eligible boundary. Check the saved return address, EOI and IRET to establish actual guest delivery.

Relevant existing tests include `sti_delays_irq_for_exactly_one_instruction_and_halt_wakes` and `v30_repc_pic_irq_between_elements_and_guest_iret` in [tests/core.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/ea2713b51a94a53232448b622f35dcb2e01b2fac/tests/core.rs), and `idtr_relocated_pic_irq_hlt_eoi_and_interrupt_shadows` in [tests/cpu386.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/ea2713b51a94a53232448b622f35dcb2e01b2fac/tests/cpu386.rs#L1467). The original [PIC guest probe](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/ea2713b51a94a53232448b622f35dcb2e01b2fac/guest/pic.asm) demonstrates guest-programmed PIT requests and IRR confirmation suitable for reuse as a testing pattern.

No supplied open Issue duplicates this behavior; the supplied completed history covers other CPU instructions and PIC operations.

Project progress: Issue #67/PR #68 added bounded channel-3 frequency selection. The [Coordinator validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/ea2713b51a94a53232448b622f35dcb2e01b2fac/docs/validation.md#issue-67-opnopna-channel-3-frequency-selection-2026-10-24) reports 280 native integration and 100 production-Wasm browser passes. Independent review and remote CI evidence were not supplied. The evaluator ran no builds, tests or fixture preparation.

Retain all 26 supplied inventory scopes and statuses: **partial** cpu-v30, cpu386, protected-mode, memory, pic, pit, dma, rtc, keyboard, mouse, fdc, ide, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, pcm86, bios, lio and integration; **implemented_unverified** grcg; **unimplemented** paging and fpu. This Issue does not complete a category.

V30 still requires packed-BCD strings, bit-field extensions, TF traps, NMI, and broader instruction/prefix/fault acceptance. Segment-shadow interactions outside this focused acceptance remain unverified. Protected execution, paging and basic x87 retain their required scopes.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add `v30_segment_irq_` Rust tests in `tests/core.rs`. Demonstrate a failing minimal reproduction against the unchanged baseline, then passing behavior after implementation. Assert guest-visible progress and PIC/frame state, rather than only the internal inhibition field.
- [ ] Cover every documented segment source/destination listed above, both register and memory MOV forms, all three segment POPs, representative default/overridden segments, and unaligned memory operands. Verify exact transfer results, FLAGS preservation and guarded memory.
- [ ] Prove the following ordinary instruction executes before acknowledgement, the PIC request remains pending during inhibition, and exactly one interrupt subsequently enters with the correct six-byte frame. Execute guest EOI/IRET and verify resumed progress. Include a changed SS followed by stack-pointer setup to check the resulting interrupt stack.
- [ ] Cover consecutive qualifying instructions, IF-clear execution, a masked request later unmasked, and reset with inhibition pending. Include ordinary MOV and PUSH-segment controls that detect accidental broad inhibition. Test at least one prefixed following instruction without granting an extra instruction of delay.
- [ ] Add `ap_v30_segment_irq_` tests in `tests/cpu386.rs` demonstrating that the VM change does not introduce inhibition after Ap non-SS segment MOV/POP forms. Preserve existing Ap SS/STI, single-step, relocated-IDTR, exception-frame and reset assertions.
- [ ] Add an original MIT guest probe, suggested path `guest/v30_segment_irq.asm`. Use guest-programmed PIT/PIC ports to establish a pending request while IF is clear, confirm IRR, then execute sequences such as `STI; MOV DS,AX; INC marker`. Check delivery ordering inside the guest handler. Include segment-read, memory, POP and consecutive-producer cases. Host-written results or direct CPU interrupt injection must not supply guest acceptance.
- [ ] Supply offline preparation and a checked provenance manifest, suggested names `tools/prepare_v30_segment_irq_fixture.py` and `fixtures/v30-segment-irq-manifest.json`. Record source/license, assembler command, source/boot/image hashes, exact results/guards and a maximum **2,000,000 scheduler slots per boot**. Use original source and synthetic firmware; require no commercial ROM or guest software. Keep generated assets outside `web/`.
- [ ] Boot the identical probe natively and through the production release-Wasm artifact at both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, before and after reset. Require a guest-produced PASS marker, exact result/guard bytes, unchanged disk bytes, bounded completion, and no FAIL, emulator or browser errors.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs the new fixture preparation and focused checks, then all applicable [README reproduction checks](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/ea2713b51a94a53232448b622f35dcb2e01b2fac/README.md#reproduce-the-checks): existing fixture prerequisites, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, font verification, `git diff --check`, and full `npm test`. Focused commands should include `cargo test --locked --test core v30_segment_irq_` and `cargo test --locked --test cpu386 ap_v30_segment_irq_`. Integrate probe preparation into acceptance CI.
- [ ] Preserve existing hardware, DOS/application, VM, audio and six-game assertions and instruction budgets. Report exact commands, failures, reruns and final results. Update hardware/validation documentation with the bounded contract and remaining gaps; do not claim full V30 accuracy or commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
